newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks flat at open, LVMH takes a beating.
newsitem.headline: French stocks flat at open, LVMH takes a beating.

text.p: The Paris bourse's blue chip CAC-40 index was little changed in early trading on Thursday as it struggled through resistance above the 2,100 level.
Several big blue chips, including LVMH and Lyonnaise des Eaux, were hammered by investors disappointed with their first-half results.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 0.14 point, or 0.1 percent, at 2,103.55 at 0900 GMT after trading in a narrow range between 2,099 and 2,106. The CAC-40 September futures contract was up two points at 2,107.
Volume was a heavy 1.4 billion francs.
Shares in LVMH were down two percent at 1,079, extending Wednesday's 2.8 percent loss.

The group reported a 5.4 percent rise in net attributable profit excluding exceptionals to 1.54 billion francs -- below most analysts' estimates. It reported a fall in operating income due to a slump in profit from perfumes unit.
Shares in Lyonnaise des Eaux fell 2.5 percent to 455.50 francs after the utilities company reported a 635 million franc profit -- slightly below estimates.

Alcatel Alsthom's stock rose 1.6 percent after the telecommunications and engineering group reported a narrower first-half loss and confirmed its objective for a full year breakeven and a 1996 profit including capital gains.
